You settle the technical terms of a partner integration from notices, agreements, partner sheets, a forum and tickets. They often disagree.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Precedence rule: when sources disagree, the order of authority is regulator-notice > master-agreement > partner-sheet > forum > ticket. Inside one source, the higher version wins.
- [e002] The master-agreement document MSA-1 (version 1) states that the text encoding is `ascii-7`.
- [e003] The master-agreement document MSA-1 (version 1) states that the compression codec is `gzip`.
- [e004] According to master-agreement MSA-1 version 1, the idle timeout in seconds is `300`.
- [e005] The master-agreement document MSA-1 (version 1) states that the primary data center is `dc-lon3`.
- [e006] The master-agreement document MSA-1 (version 1) states that the audit trail mode is `ON`.
- [e007] The master-agreement document MSA-1 (version 1) states that the burst quota per minute is `350`.
- [e008] According to partner-sheet PS-129 version 2, the backup interval in hours is `6`.

Sources, from highest to lowest authority: regulator-notice, master-agreement, partner-sheet, forum, ticket. When two sources disagree, the higher one decides.
Inside one source, a higher version number overrides a lower one. A withdrawn document no longer counts at all.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
